title: Sharing my Gen AI workflow for animating my sprite in Spine2D. It's very manual because i wanted precise control of attack timings and locations.
author: Selphea

comments.author: rvitor
comments.body: Could you give more details about the body parts, did you manually cut the parts to animate it? How did it turn out, if you did that?

replies.author: Selphea
replies.body:
That was all hand redrawn. I needed to do that to control the flow of hair and make sure parts could be separated to over/under layers e.g. sleeve over hand, hair over face while making sure the parts underneath are complete if the upper layer moves. The layer breakdown is on the right side.

Hypothetically, Qwen Image or Nano Banana might be able to slice for you, though it's hit or miss with Qwen missing a little more. Or a ComfyUI inpainting workflow to clear out the upper layers e.g. having a head without the hair. The fully automated way would be to just let the AI do everything and give you frame by frame output, though stability and precision will be an issue.

replies.body: I'm actually manually animating because there's some backend stuff that needs specific events in animation. But [https://x.com/chongdashu](https://x.com/chongdashu) is working on AI-generated animation.

replies.author: fourmigothacked
replies.body: I know you are, but I try also with spine2d but chatGPT cut the part of the body very bad right now how do you do it?

replies.author: Selphea
replies.body: If you use an easy to animate style like anime coloring or cel shading then it's easier to manually extend or edit parts.

replies.author: Selphea
replies.body: Option A is use a vector tool like Inkscape or Illustrator if the style is a lot of solid colors. Option 2 is to do full raster using Krita with Comfy plugin to inpaint the bad sections, but it's a bit of a gamble.

replies.author: Selphea
replies.body:
The most promising solution right now is Shitagaki Lab's See-through: https://github.com/shitagaki-lab/see-through

Depending on how much motion you need it might be enough. If you need full motion then you'll need to refine it more.
